memory_title: Search visibility is not traversal coverage
durable_memory: Repository code search, commit search, direct immutable-object inspection, and branch-name search are distinct evidence modalities. Their union can establish candidate presence, rejection boundaries, and temporal upper bounds, but cannot establish exhaustive branch or reachable-history coverage unless the client retains a complete ref inventory and a traversal ledger proving every reachable commit was visited. Zero results from branch-name or indexed search are therefore capability-bounded observations, not evidence that no branch or historical assignment exists.

observed: The canonical queue still requires an exhaustive branch inventory or equivalent repository history traversal before M-004, M-005, or M-006 may be classified as unlocated.
Authenticated commit search for M-004 returned only downstream continuity reconciliation commits, including unresolved-origin, temporal-boundary, collision-rejection, and search-coverage records.
A branch-name search with an empty query returned no branch records in this run.
Direct inspection of commit 114d63cb2723fcf7dfc879819de31d44e076899e confirms that the first located immutable objects are temporal upper bounds, not accepted origins.
The current connector surface used in this run did not produce a complete ref list, reachable-commit set, deleted-path ledger, or proof that all branches were traversed.
inferred: Search-index completeness and repository-graph completeness are independent properties.
A zero-result branch-name search cannot be promoted into a one-branch inventory without an explicit completeness guarantee from the retrieval method.
Candidate discovery can advance rejection and temporal constraints even when origin resolution remains fail-closed.
proposed: Represent exhaustive repository coverage as a retained traversal envelope containing ref enumeration method, complete ref set, root commit set, visited commit set, parent-edge closure, historical path queries, deleted-path evidence, retrieval timestamps, and canonical digests.

Require the traversal envelope to report no unvisited reachable commits and no unresolved ref-pagination or permission blind spots before permitting verified_origin or unlocated_after_exhaustive_coverage.
Continue using indexed search and immutable commit inspection only as candidate and contradiction-discovery inputs, never as substitutes for graph traversal.
superseded: Treating zero branch-search results as proof that only the default branch exists.
Treating commit-search silence before a temporal boundary as exhaustive absence.
Combining several bounded search modalities and calling the result exhaustive without a retained closure proof.
unresolved: The complete reachable-commit graph and deleted-path history preceding the three temporal upper bounds.
The originating decision log, language lexicon, project document, or privacy-reviewed chat locator for M-004, M-005, and M-006.

contradiction_resolution.apparent_conflict: Several authenticated searches can return no earlier assignment while the provenance outcome remains unresolved.
contradiction_resolution.resolution: Authenticated search establishes trustworthy observations about returned results, not completeness of the repository graph. Provenance remains unresolved until coverage completeness is separately proven.

does_not_support: complete ref inventory without an explicit exhaustive contract

sources: authenticated GitHub commit search for M-004
falsification_route: Produce an authenticated retrieval contract demonstrating that the branch search used here returns the complete ref inventory for an empty query.
Retain a complete ref and reachable-commit traversal envelope and show that indexed search alone yields the same closed set under all historical and deleted-path cases.
Locate an immutable pre-boundary assignment satisfying exact identifier, namespace, owner, semantic role, temporal precedence, and immutable locator agreement.
